articles.deck: How ministerial direction drove a $4.8-billion community lab outsourcing commitment without a documented business case—leaving taxpayers with an estimated $77 million in extra costs, a buyout cheque, and restricted audit records.
articles.title: No Documented Business Case, One Bidder, and a $31.5-Million Buyback: Inside Alberta's DynaLIFE Reversal

entries.attribution: Alberta Health Services audited 2023–24 annual report

citations.locator: printed p. 127, note 27, row Cash purchase consideration paid ($31,500 thousand)
printed p. 127, note 27, row Net balances due from DLDX settled at acquisition ($16,295 thousand)

entries.summary: AHS’s audited statements report $31.5 million cash purchase consideration for acquiring DynaLIFE operations on August 31, 2023, after settling $16.295 million in balances due from DynaLIFE. The same transaction appears as $29.388 million net cash outflow after cash acquired. The legal cash payee and owner-level distribution are unverified.
entries.title: $31.5 million disclosed cash purchase consideration ($29.388M net cash outflow)

entries.attribution: Auditor General of Alberta; Premier Danielle Smith in Hansard

citations.locator: printed p. 2, Access to Information Challenges
printed pp. 395–396, Oral Question Period, Premier Smith

entries.summary: The Auditor General said AHS restricted access to records with Department of Health support and that the impact of missing or redacted material was indeterminate. Premier Smith told the Assembly the government fully cooperated and disputed suggestions otherwise. The available records do not establish personal intent behind the access limits.
entries.title: Dispute over records access during the Auditor General examination

entries.attribution: AHS Board minutes; Auditor General of Alberta

citations.locator: PDF p. 4, Finance Committee item 2(a), resolution 3
PDF p. 3, Finance Committee item 2(a), motion

entries.summary: AHS’s board unanimously approved AHS and APL entering a DynaLIFE term sheet on January 27, 2022 and conditionally delegated CEO authority to execute a later services agreement if its final fundamental terms were not substantively different. The Auditor General separately reports board approval of the contract based on value. The final condition and signatories remain unverified.
entries.title: AHS board term-sheet approval and conditional CEO delegation

entries.summary: The Auditor General found no evidence that AHS or Alberta Health developed a formal business case before initiating the procurement. This is an audit finding subject to the auditor’s stated indeterminate access limitation, not proof that no other analysis existed.
entries.title: Absence of a documented formal business case (OAG finding)

citations.locator: printed p. 35, Cost to Alberta Taxpayers
printed pp. 34–35, Cost to Alberta Taxpayers

entries.summary: The Auditor General estimated about $61 million in incremental cost against an estimated continuation of the prior service model over roughly eight months, plus $16 million to reintegrate services, producing $77 million for the 2019–23 initiative. These are audit-assessed additional costs, not gross payments to DynaLIFE.
entries.title: $77 million auditor-estimated extra cost for 2019–23 initiative

entries.attribution: AHS; Auditor General of Alberta; Premier Danielle Smith in Hansard

citations.locator: printed p. 397, Oral Question Period, Premier Smith

entries.summary: AHS described improving service delivery as the purpose of bringing DynaLIFE operations under APL in 2023. The Auditor General reports that savings were the primary earlier objective of outsourcing. Premier Smith later said her government reversed course after seeing DynaLIFE could not manage provincewide service.
entries.title: AHS and Premier Smith rationale for outsourcing and reversal

entries.summary: The Auditor General found that the then health minister and Department of Health expected the 2019–22 community laboratory outsourcing to proceed, while AHS management and board were not the strategic decision-makers. This finding does not attribute initiation to Danielle Smith.
entries.title: Ministerial and department strategic direction (OAG finding)

entries.attribution: Alberta Health Services audited annual reports
entries.summary: AHS reported executing the services and ancillary agreements on May 30, 2022, with an estimated $4.8 billion commitment over an initial 14 years and four months. The related commitment ended on August 31, 2023. This was a prospective contract estimate, not cash paid.
entries.title: $4.8 billion estimated initial commitment (cancelled August 31, 2023)

entries.summary: The Auditor General found the written RFP met applicable document standards. After Sonic Healthcare withdrew citing pandemic travel restrictions, an independent procurement adviser said AHS could negotiate with the remaining qualified proponent. This did not resolve the auditor’s separate concerns about proceeding with one bidder.
entries.title: Written RFP met standards; Sonic withdrew citing pandemic travel limits

entries.attribution: Auditor General of Alberta; AHS audited 2023–24 financial statements

citations.locator: printed pp. 34–35, Cost to Alberta Taxpayers

entries.next_check: Obtain executed 2022 agreement and amendments, AHS/APL service-payment remittance ledger, acquisition closing reconciliation, and certified Alberta Corporate Registry partnership searches.
entries.summary: Public financial statements and the Auditor General examination do not disclose total gross service payments to DynaLIFE under the expanded 2022 agreement, the executed contract text or board-condition check, or the legal cash payee and owner-level distribution of the $31.5 million acquisition consideration.
entries.title: Gross service payments, contract terms, and owner-level proceeds remain unverified

blocks.heading: Decision and countercontext
blocks.text: The Auditor General examined how Alberta Health and AHS proceeded with expanded community laboratory outsourcing between 2019 and 2023, alongside the compliant written RFP finding and government rationale.

blocks.heading: Separate money measures
blocks.text: Public records report three distinct financial measures that answer different questions and must not be summed: a cancelled $4.8 billion prospective commitment, $77 million in auditor-estimated extra costs, and $31.5 million in disclosed cash purchase consideration.

pages.summary: Public-record overview of how Alberta directed, contracted, and reversed expanded community lab outsourcing.
pages.title: DynaLIFE community lab contract — overview

scope.coverage: Public-record slice of Alberta's 2019–23 DynaLIFE community laboratory contract from the November 2025 Auditor General examination, AHS audited FY 2022–23 and 2023–24 financial statements, January 27, 2022 public AHS board minutes, and November 20, 2025 Alberta Hansard. Former-vendor operational claims remain privately held pending outreach.

images.alt: Dark charcoal editorial magazine cover titled Alberta's DynaLIFE Playbook — File #01: No documented business case. One bidder. A $31.5M buyback. Satirical illustration shows a brass seesaw on a glowing teal medical-cross fulcrum slammed down by chained, redacted, crimson-bowed contract folders with a cracked smoking piggy bank, launching a rack of blood-sample test tubes and a crumpled napkin into the air.
images.label: Cover: Alberta's DynaLIFE Playbook (File #01)

images.alt: Editorial comic panel 1 of 4 titled Step 1: Skip the Homework. A smiling cartoon official throws blank pages out a boardroom window while pointing to a crumpled napkin as a stunned analyst searches the empty table with a magnifying glass. Caption notes the Auditor General found no documented formal business case from AHS or Alberta Health before procurement began.
images.label: Panel 1/4: Step 1 — Skip the Homework

images.alt: Editorial comic panel 2 of 4 titled Step 2: The One-Bidder Auction. A rival bidder dashes out an exit door with a suitcase while one lone corporate bidder lounges with feet up holding an auction paddle as an auctioneer bangs a gavel beside a tray of glass lab test tubes. Caption notes Sonic Healthcare exited over pandemic travel curbs, leaving one bidder for a $4.8B prospective commitment.
images.label: Panel 2/4: Step 2 — The One-Bidder Auction

images.alt: Editorial comic panel 3 of 4 titled Step 3: Pay to Buy It Back. An exhausted health official hands a giant ribboned envelope across a counter for a wooden crate of lab test tubes while a tipped piggy bank smokes behind him. Caption separates the Auditor General's $77M extra-cost estimate from AHS's $31.5M buyout cash paid.
images.label: Panel 3/4: Step 3 — Pay to Buy It Back

images.alt: Editorial comic panel 4 of 4 titled Step 4: Full Cooperation. A bewildered auditor examines a chained, redacted filing cabinet with a magnifying glass while a cheerful official gives a thumbs-up leaning on a broom beside a lumpy rug hiding folders. Caption cites the Auditor General's restricted-access finding alongside Premier Smith's Hansard statement that the government cooperated fully.
images.label: Panel 4/4: Step 4 — Full Cooperation
